questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\coordinate (O) at (0,0);\coordinate (R) at (3.4525,0);\coordinate (T) at (0,2.444);\draw (O)--(R);\draw (O)--(T) node[midway,left] {$5.2\text{ m}$};\draw (R)--(T) node[midway,above right] {$9.0\text{ m}$};\coordinate (va) at ($(O)!0.3cm!(R)$);\coordinate (vb) at ($(O)!0.3cm!(T)$);\draw (va)--($(va)+(vb)-(O)$)--(vb);\pic[draw,"$\theta$",angle radius=0.62cm,angle eccentricity=1.5] {angle=T--R--O};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Find $\theta$, correct to the nearest degree.

options.why: Used $\cos^{-1}$, treating the $5.2$ m side as adjacent to $\theta$ when it is opposite.
Used $\tan^{-1}$, treating the $9.0$ m hypotenuse as the adjacent side.
Inverted the ratio to $\frac{9.0}{5.2}$ and used $\tan^{-1}$.

[/tikz]
Find $\theta$, correct to the nearest degree.

options.why: Used $\sin^{-1}$, treating the $15$ cm side as opposite $\theta$ when it is adjacent.
Used $\tan^{-1}$, treating the $17$ cm hypotenuse as the side opposite $\theta$.

questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\coordinate (O) at (0,0);\coordinate (L) at (-3.85,0);\coordinate (T) at (0,2.31);\draw (O)--(L) node[midway,below] {$7.0\text{ cm}$};\draw (O)--(T) node[midway,right] {$4.2\text{ cm}$};\draw (L)--(T);\coordinate (va) at ($(O)!0.3cm!(L)$);\coordinate (vb) at ($(O)!0.3cm!(T)$);\draw (va)--($(va)+(vb)-(O)$)--(vb);\pic[draw,"$\theta$",angle radius=0.75cm,angle eccentricity=1.45] {angle=O--L--T};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Find $\theta$, correct to the nearest degree.

options.why: Inverted the ratio to $\frac{7.0}{4.2}$, swapping the opposite and adjacent sides.
Used $\sin^{-1}$, treating the $7.0$ cm adjacent side as the hypotenuse.
Used $\cos^{-1}$ on the two legs, as though $4.2$ cm were the hypotenuse.

questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\coordinate (O) at (0,0);\coordinate (R) at (1.19,0);\coordinate (T) at (0,4.08);\draw (O)--(R) node[midway,below] {$7\text{ mm}$};\draw (O)--(T) node[midway,left] {$24\text{ mm}$};\draw (R)--(T) node[midway,above right] {$25\text{ mm}$};\coordinate (va) at ($(O)!0.28cm!(R)$);\coordinate (vb) at ($(O)!0.28cm!(T)$);\draw (va)--($(va)+(vb)-(O)$)--(vb);\pic[draw,"$\theta$",angle radius=0.55cm,angle eccentricity=1.6] {angle=T--R--O};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
All three sides are given.
Find $\theta$, correct to the nearest degree.

options.why: Swapped the opposite and adjacent sides, using $\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{7}{24}\right)$.
Used the $25$ mm hypotenuse as the adjacent side, giving $\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{24}{25}\right)$.

questions.solution_text:
Relative to $\theta$ the $24$ mm side is opposite and the $7$ mm side is adjacent.
$\tan\theta=\frac{24}{7}$
$\theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{24}{7}\right)$
$=73.7397\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx74^{\circ}$

Read the decimal part of $42.6^{\circ}$ straight off as $6$ minutes instead of converting it.

[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\coordinate (L) at (0,0);\coordinate (O) at (3.08,0);\coordinate (T) at (3.08,2.38);\draw (L)--(O) node[midway,below] {$1.1\text{ m}$};\draw (O)--(T) node[midway,right] {$0.85\text{ m}$};\draw[very thick] (L)--(T);\coordinate (va) at ($(O)!0.3cm!(L)$);\coordinate (vb) at ($(O)!0.3cm!(T)$);\draw (va)--($(va)+(vb)-(O)$)--(vb);\pic[draw,"$\theta$",angle radius=0.7cm,angle eccentricity=1.5] {angle=O--L--T};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
A short staircase rises $0.85$ m over a horizontal run of $1.1$ m. Find $\theta$, the angle the staircase makes with the floor, correct to the nearest degree.

options.why: Swapped the rise and the run, using $\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1.1}{0.85}\right)$.
Truncated $37.69^{\circ}$ instead of rounding it up.
Used $\sin^{-1}$, treating the $1.1$ m run as the sloping length of the staircase.

questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\coordinate (O) at (0,0);\coordinate (R) at (3.92933,0);\coordinate (T) at (0,1.98);\draw (O)--(R);\draw (O)--(T) node[midway,left] {$9\text{ cm}$};\draw (R)--(T) node[midway,above right] {$20\text{ cm}$};\coordinate (va) at ($(O)!0.3cm!(R)$);\coordinate (vb) at ($(O)!0.3cm!(T)$);\draw (va)--($(va)+(vb)-(O)$)--(vb);\pic[draw,"$\theta$",angle radius=0.7cm,angle eccentricity=1.5] {angle=T--R--O};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Which expression gives $\theta$?

options.why: Left out the inverse, so this evaluates a ratio rather than undoing the sine.
Put the hypotenuse on top; a sine ratio can never exceed $1$.
Chose cosine even though the $9$ cm side is opposite $\theta$, not adjacent to it.

questions.solution_text:
The $9$ cm side is opposite $\theta$ and the $20$ cm side is the hypotenuse.
$\sin\theta=\frac{9}{20}$
$\theta=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{9}{20}\right)$

questions.question_text:
Slide A drops $2.2$ m over a sloping surface $5.0$ m long.
Slide B drops $1.6$ m over a horizontal run of $3.4$ m. Which slide is steeper, and by how many degrees, correct to the nearest degree?

options.why: Used $\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2.2}{5.0}\right)$ for slide A, treating its $5.0$ m sloping surface as a horizontal run.
Used $\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{1.6}{3.4}\right)$ for slide B, treating its $3.4$ m horizontal run as the sloping surface.

questions.solution_text:
$\sin A=\frac{2.2}{5.0}$
$A=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{2.2}{5.0}\right)$
$=26.1038\ldots^{\circ}$
$\tan B=\frac{1.6}{3.4}$
$B=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1.6}{3.4}\right)$
$=25.2010\ldots^{\circ}$
$A-B=0.9027\ldots^{\circ}$
Slide A is the steeper slide, by $1^{\circ}$.
